page.title: Daily Report
page.description: AI-generated technical reports that analyze current systems evidence, identify research gaps, and propose testable ideas with academic and production value. These pages are not human-reviewed.
page.bodyHtml:
Eunomia Daily Report is a separate publication stream for AI-generated technical analysis. Each report starts from a concrete systems question, compares primary evidence, identifies what current research or production practice still fails to explain, and proposes ideas that could be tested as research systems or deployed as engineering mechanisms.

Every page in this section is generated by AI and has not received human editorial review. Citations, facts, measurements, interpretations, and proposed directions may contain errors. Readers should inspect the primary sources and independently verify any conclusion before using it in production or an important decision.

These reports are analysis drafts for readers, not peer-reviewed papers and not statements endorsed by a human author.

Current reports

When Several AI Agents Work at Once, Who Makes Sure the Final Result Is Right?

Worktrees, sandboxes, and parallel tool calls can isolate workers while still producing a wrong combined outcome. This report uses code changes, shared budgets, approvals, and irreversible actions to explain why parallel agents need one validation and commit step before their effects become real. It also identifies missing benchmarks and effect contracts, then proposes an agent transaction layer, a semantic-conflict benchmark, and adaptive concurrency control.

What Should an AI Agent Trace Keep? Observability Under a Fixed Evidence Budget

AI agent traces can generate hundreds of system events around each model call while still omitting decisive state, authority, or provenance. This report develops an evidence-portfolio architecture and then identifies open problems in evidence utility, portable schemas, unbiased adaptive capture, and equal-budget evaluation.

Publication contract

A Daily Report should provide more than a fluent literature summary. It should contain:

  • a concrete question that affects a real systems or engineering decision;
  • an opening that a technically qualified reader can understand without reading the source corpus;
  • independent primary evidence and clear separation between measured facts and generated interpretation;
  • a real disagreement, missing mechanism, deployment failure, or unexplained boundary;
  • explicit assumptions, uncertainty, applicability limits, and falsification conditions;
  • a section that states where current research or production practice remains weak;
  • a section proposing a small number of non-trivial ideas, each with a mechanism, novelty claim, implementable artifact, evaluation plan, academic value, production value, and failure condition;
  • an explicit disclosure that the page is AI-generated and not human-reviewed.

The Blog remains the archive for project writing, tutorials, releases, engineering explanations, and editorial articles. Daily Report stays separate so automated analysis is never presented as human-reviewed Eunomia research.
